title: Staged constraint validator and deterministic fallback harness for routing policies
creator: Asha Patel
description: Refactor the routing policy validation path to introduce a staged constraint validator and a deterministic fallback verification harness. The goal is to make region selection, tier routing, and model-variant fallback behavior provably safe under common failure modes (region outage, capacity throttling, model variant mismatch). Deliver a pluggable validator pipeline that can run incremental checks at config-load, deploy-time, and runtime admission. Provide a harness to run deterministic simulation scenarios (region failure, tier saturation, partial capacity) against the current policy set so we can assert and trace fallback decisions before rollout.
acceptance_criteria: Validator pipeline accepts a policy config with staged checks: syntax -> type coercion -> referential integrity -> capacity constraints -> deterministic fallback sanity; failing checks produce actionable error messages and suggested fixes.
A deterministic harness can simulate at least three failure modes (region down, tier overloaded, model variant unavailable) and produce a decision trace for every request route evaluated.

All existing routing config fixtures (50+ canonical samples) pass the new validator with identical effective route semantics unless intentionally flagged; delta reports must be generated for configs whose semantics would change.
Integration tests added: 12 end-to-end scenarios validating region selection + tier routing + fallback to variant/region with expected metrics (latency penalty, fallback count) asserted.
Validator is pluggable and registered in the runtime pipeline; we ship a feature-flagged rollout to 10% of traffic and capture trace logs in staging before full release.
Performance: validator admission latency for a single config load < 120ms median; harness simulation for a policy < 2s per scenario when using cached model metadata.
Documentation: Confluence spec + example migration guide and CLI tool docs for running the harness locally are published and linked.
tasks: Design staged validator API and registry (syntax, schema, referential, constraints, fallback-safety).
Implement syntax and schema checkers using existing parser module (reuse token locations for errors).
Add referential integrity layer to verify model ids, region names, tier ids against runtime catalog (with cache TTL).
Implement fallback-safety checker: for every route, enumerate fallback variants and verify that at least one compatible variant exists per failure-mode policy.
Build deterministic harness: scenario definitions, simulated capacity maps, and decision trace output format (JSONL).
Wire validator into config push CI: run validator in pre-merge checks and as part of canary deployment job.
Add integration tests exercising region down, partial capacity, and slow-region latency fallbacks; add to e2e suite.
Create migration report script that compares old vs new routing semantics and highlights changes with remediation suggestions.
Performance tune: profile validator path and add caching layers where safe (model metadata, region maps).
Write Confluence spec and CLI usage docs for the harness; include example scenarios for common customer topologies.
notes: Rationale: current policy validation is ad-hoc and scattered between the control plane and runtime. This leads to surprises on rollout and makes rollback decisions difficult.
We must ensure deterministic ordering of checks so that error messages are stable and useful to PMs and SREs.
A pluggable design will let product teams opt into stricter constraint sets (enterprise customers require stronger guarantees).
We should align trace formats with console rollout traces (add route_id, policy_version, scenario_id) so Console can render simulated decision flows.
Cross-team owners: Runtime (Miguel), Policy UI (Lena Fischer), Console tracing (Owen Park), QA (Priya Menon).
Risk: too-strict referential checks could break older deploys; mitigations include a compatibility mode and migration reports.
